faq.q: Where does the conversion happen — is my video uploaded?
faq.a: No upload. Your video is read with the browser's file API and converted on your device using gif.js; only the library itself is downloaded to you. On first visit it fetches gif.js and JSZip, after which they're cached. The GIF worker is loaded by fetching the script and running it from a same-origin blob, since browsers refuse to build a worker from a cross-origin URL.

faq.q: What quality presets and controls are available?
faq.a: Four presets: Small (240p, 8 FPS), Medium (360p, 10 FPS), High (480p, 15 FPS), and Original (full width, 15 FPS). You can also set FPS (5–30), output width (100–1200px), speed (0.5x–2x), and loop count (infinite, 1, 3, or 5). A live size estimate updates from your trim length, FPS, width, and play mode.

faq.q: What do the play modes and text overlay do?
faq.a: Play mode offers Normal, Reverse, and Boomerang (plays forward then backward). You can add an optional text overlay and place it in one of seven positions (corners, centers) — it's drawn with a white fill and black outline onto each frame. A trim timeline with draggable handles lets you pick the start and end; the tool suggests keeping clips under about 10 seconds.

faq.q: Can I save individual frames or copy the GIF?
faq.a: After converting, the 'GIF + frames (ZIP)' button bundles the finished animation.gif plus every captured frame as numbered PNGs using JSZip, reusing frames already in memory. The Copy button copies only the first frame as a PNG and says so plainly, because browsers can't copy animated GIFs to the clipboard. You can also download the GIF directly.
